component.name: Blick
component.summary: View, rotate and upload pictures to Immich

description.p: Blick shows a folder as a contact sheet: every picture side by side, numbered in folder order. Double-click opens a picture large, and the arrow keys page through the rest.

ul.li: Reads JPEG, PNG, WebP, TIFF, HEIC, AVIF, JPEG XL and camera RAW from Canon, Nikon, Sony, Fujifilm, Panasonic, Olympus and others.
Library: search folders like Photos recursively, every subfolder shows up as an album.
Rotate several pictures left or right at once. Blick rotates JPEG files losslessly through the EXIF orientation, RAW files through an XMP file next to them.
Looks from .cube LUTs, HaldCLUTs (such as RawTherapee's film simulations) and Lightroom presets, with a strength slider, for many pictures at once too.
Adjust brightness, contrast and saturation with a live preview and save the result as a copy.
Upload pictures to Immich, straight into an album if you like.
Browse Immich albums, even very large ones, month by month.
Play videos, local and from Immich, muted at the start.
Find duplicates in the spirit of dupeGuru: identical files, similar pictures, similar file names and matching folders, also on network shares (SMB, SFTP, WebDAV) and in Immich.

description.p: The whole app is now in English: interface, messages, code comments and metadata. Looks saved by earlier versions in sidecars keep working.
First public release on GitHub. New app ID io.github.paulhoever.Blick so Blick installs cleanly outside a home network. Settings and data of the earlier ID are not carried over.
README rewritten, screenshots in the repository, no references to internal servers left in code and metadata.
The JPEG XL conversion now always converts WebP and HEIC, even if the file gets larger, because many programs can't read these formats. JPEG and PNG stay as they are if JPEG XL saves nothing.

New in the main menu: "Convert folder to JPEG XL". JPEG is repacked losslessly (restorable bit for bit), PNG losslessly, WebP and HEIC only if the conversion comes out smaller. EXIF is kept, and the originals go to the trash if you want.
USB sticks and SD cards show up in the sidebar. The duplicate comparison has a close button and shows all pictures of the group instead of just two.

Double-clicking a picture now opens it in the viewer right away, without loading the folder as a contact sheet. Several selected pictures can be paged through with the arrow keys. Only the way back loads the folder. The file association also knows more formats (PNM, ICO, DDS, HDR).

Duplicate search (menu, Ctrl+Shift+D): four search modes as in dupeGuru, namely identical content, similar pictures (even rotated or cropped), similar file names and matching folders. Locations can be folders, network shares (SMB, SFTP, WebDAV) and the Immich library; reference folders are never suggested for deletion.

Fast, because size, partial hash and index skip most comparisons and all checksums and picture signatures are cached: the second run is done almost instantly. On servers Blick reads only a few hundred KB per file, and nothing at all from Immich.
Cleaning up: mark (all but the best, by path part), side-by-side comparison, move to trash, move, replace with a hardlink, delete permanently and export as CSV.
Zooming with the keys (+, −, 1) and the zoom buttons now targets the mouse position instead of the image center. Ctrl+scroll, pinch and double-click already did.
While the full resolution of an Immich picture is still loading, a notice with a spinner at the bottom left shows the progress.

Videos now also play under Wayland with a real GPU. Before, they didn't load there at all, because a rotation filter pinned playback to system memory. The display now rotates portrait videos correctly by itself.
Videos can no longer be rotated or given a look; that only works for photos. Deleting and uploading stay.

In the Immich sheet, right-click or long press offers "Download …" for one or more pictures and "Copy share link". While scrolling, a badge shows the month, and the calendar button jumps straight to a year and month.

Videos: Blick shows them in the contact sheet with a still frame and plays them in the single view, local and from Immich. A plain player with play/pause and volume, every video starts muted. Space plays or pauses, M toggles sound, arrow up and down change the volume.
From Immich it plays the version the server already converted for the browser. Blick itself converts nothing.

Cropping: free or with aspect ratio presets (original, 1:1, 4:3, 3:2, 16:9, 5:4, 7:5, 2:1), landscape or portrait. The frame can be dragged by its corners and edges, moved, and nudged with the keyboard (C starts, Enter applies). Like the adjustments, the crop goes into the copy, into the original, or is remembered next to the picture, and it rotates along when you rotate.
Also: pictures from Immich arrive in full resolution after the preview, HEIC too. If the server has no large version, Blick fetches the original and decodes it itself.

New look following the GNOME guidelines: stock libadwaita instead of custom colors and corners, rounded prints, round buttons over the picture, zoom buttons at the bottom right, an edit bar with groups, a shortcuts overview (Ctrl+?), a new app icon. Below 500 pixels of width the selection bar shows only icons, so Blick fits narrow screens too.
Also: while editing, a long press on the picture shows the original.

RAW, HEIC, AVIF and JPEG XL, a library with subfolders as albums, looks, zoom, fullscreen, picture info, trash with undo, folder watching, remembering settings next to the picture, downloading originals from Immich.
Also: RAW develop matched to the camera preview, lossless rotation of HEIC, AVIF and JPEG XL, thumbnails with remembered adjustments and looks, space bar as quick look, light/dark in the main menu.
First version: contact sheet, single view, adjustments, batch rotation, Immich upload and albums.
